newsitem.title: USA: LG&E to buy KU Energy for $1.54 billion.
newsitem.headline: LG&E to buy KU Energy for $1.54 billion.

text.p: LG&E Energy Corp. said on Wednesday it reached a definitive agreement to acquire KU Energy Corp., another Kentucky utility, in a deal worth about $1.54 billion.

The new holding company, to be called LG&E Energy and based in Louisville, would serve 1.1 million customers in Kentucky, Virginia and internationally. Its combined revenues in 1996 would have been more than $4.3 billion.

The agreement, which is expected to be tax-free, calls for KU Energy shareholders to receive 1.67 shares of LG&E common stock for each KU share. The companies said the deal would marginally dilute earnings in the first year after the merger, but would be accretive after that.

Based on Tuesday's closing price of $24.375 for LG&E's stock, each share of KU would be worth $40.70. KU, based in Lexington, Ky., closed Tuesday at $30.375. Both issues trade on the New York Stock Exchange.

The companies said they expect to reap more than $760 million in gross non-fuel savings over 10 years as a result of the deal, which is subject to approval by regulators and the companies' shareholders.

The companies said they do not expect to seek any base rate increases over the next five years. The efficiences created by the merger should reduce customers' bills nearly 2 percent for each of those five years, they added.
